subject: Private vs Dedicated: sizing and procurement checklist for MedSecure pilot
messages:
From: Claire Adams <claire@medsecure.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romsecure.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask: private deployment sizing and timeline

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the MedSecure engineering team liked the latency profile for the chat flows. We have a short internal procurement window and some regulatory constraints (data residency in us-west, encrypted key management, quarterly audit log exports). Before we loop procurement, can you help with two things?

1) A concise comparison of what Redwood would size and deliver for a dedicated (reserved) capacity plan vs a Private (customer VPC) deployment for a 3-month pilot (expected 50k queries/day, 90% under 256 tokens). Please call out: GPU classes you recommend, expected p95 latency, and lead time for provisioning.
2) A simple mutual action plan for procurement and security review we can share with our compliance team.

I attached our initial security questionnaire (some fields blank) — Alex will fill in the compliance contacts.

Can you get a short proposal and MAP by next Tuesday? Procurement is targeting a decision by 03/29.

Claire
Director, Platform Engineering
MedSecure Health

Claire — great to hear the demo landed well. Thanks for sending the questionnaire. I looped in Markus (product/infra) and Laura (CS) to make sure we capture handoff and SLOs.

High level summary up front: for the workload profile you described (50k QPD, short sequences), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) will be faster to provision and lower operational friction; Private (VPC) gives stronger isolation and control for audits but has longer lead times for on-prem or air-gapped setups.

Deliverables we will share by Tue 23 Mar:
- One-page Private vs Dedicated comparison (recommended GPU families, p95 latency estimates, cost delta)
- Mutual action plan with milestones for procurement, security review, and pilot runbook
- Initial sizing worksheet and recommended provisioning timeline

Quick question for scoping: are you planning to bring your own HSM/KMS, or do you want Redwood to manage keys in a customer-dedicated KMS integration? That affects the private deployment path and estimated lead time.

I'll attach the one-pager and a draft MAP.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Pilot ask: private deployment sizing and timeline

Claire / team — adding technical color and a recommended sizing concrete enough for procurement estimates.

Assumptions (confirmable):
- 50k queries/day, diurnal pattern with 60% of traffic in a 10-hour business window
- 90% < 256 tokens, tail 10% up to 1024 tokens
- Model: mid-sized _llm-qa-2b_ equivalent; suggestion to test both quantized and FP16 variants during pilot

Dedicated (reserved capacity) proposal:
- Fleet: 6 x 80GB A100 GPUs (NVIDIA A100 80GB) in reserved pool, autoscale + 2 burst nodes
- Expected p95 latency: ~120–200ms for 256-token calls; 250–400ms tail for longer sequences
- Throughput: ~120–160 concurrent short requests sustained with batching
- Lead time: 1–2 weeks to allocate reserved capacity in our hosted region
- Pros: fast provisioning, cost-effective for predictable load, Redwood manages runtime and kernels
- Cons: less control over network isolation compared to VPC/private control plane

Private (VPC/air-gapped) proposal:
- Fleet options (customer-managed or Redwood-installed):
  - Minimal pilot: 4 x H100 80GB nodes (better perf for long sequences) or 8 x L4 (cost-efficient inference) depending on model choice
  - Expected p95 latency: H100 setup ~90–180ms; L4 ~130–260ms (varies by quantization)
- Throughput: depends on node choice; H100 gives higher concurrency and better KV cache performance
- Lead time: 4–8 weeks for VPC integrations, 6–12 weeks for on-prem/air-gapped (procurement, network, KMS, curling images)
- Pros: full auditability, network isolation, KMS/HSM integrations in-customer control
- Cons: longer procurement & install timeline, variant operational responsibilities for MedSecure

Recommendation for pilot: start with Dedicated reserved capacity (6 x A100) for a 6-week pilot to validate latency/cost. In parallel, run a parallel Private sizing project to prepare for a hardened production cutover (if compliance requires). This hybrid timeline lets procurement meet the 03/29 decision and gives compliance the artifacts they need.

Stephanie — can you add an itemized checklist for KMS/HSM requirements and the SOC artifacts we will need to provide?

-Markus
VP Product, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot ask: private deployment sizing and timeline

Thanks Monica and Markus — this is exactly the clarity we needed. The hybrid recommendation aligns with our procurement guardrails: move fast with a reserved pilot while we complete the private deployment checklist. A few follow-ups:

- We will proceed with the Dedicated pilot (6 x A100) for initial validation. Procurement needs a one-page MOP (milestone-oriented plan) with purchase order language, rough pricing band, and a DocuSign-ready statement of work. Can you attach a DocuSign-ready SOW?
- On KMS: MedSecure will supply the HSM-managed keys; we need Redwood to confirm steps for KMS integration and whether any agent installation is required in our VPC.
- Compliance wants the initial SOC artifacts and the list of logs (what fields, retention defaults). Can Stephanie own this checklist and share a single PDF we can drop into our vendor review?

Desired timing: procurement reviews week of 03/29 and wants final SOW by 03/26 EOD. Can you confirm internal approval to produce a DocuSign SOW and the MAP by 03/26?

Claire
